summary: M1: a flood's time history. GET /api/floods/{id}/timeline lists every satellite pass over the flood's window (10 days before its start to now; past floods to 3 days after their last NWS product; at most 45 days), each read once and locked to its own granules, with its own time, platform, view shares (clear / cloud / no data), water area, a 2D PNG (GET /api/floods/{id}/passes/{key}.png) and its own SAT_CAVEAT; passes with no view (under 1 % seen clearly) are listed and marked, never drawn as water; reads run in the background with a 20 s answer budget (complete: false until done) and keep 8 Earthdata GIS request slots free for the satellite route. The same answer lists every version of every NWS product of the flood (IEM archive, every segment, plus NWS's live CAP copies, de-duplicated), verbatim, each with shown_from_ms / shown_until_ms / replaced_ms. The bundle keeps timeline.json and the classes of the 8 newest usable passes (layers/water_pass_<key>.bin). M2: 3D terrain products in the flood bundle (manifest.terrain3d): relief near the mapped water and the suggested height boost (x1.5..x10, rule written down), HAND from the bundle DEM and NOAA NWM river lines (now fetched by the build), and the FwDET depth estimate (Cohen et al. 2018, 2019) for the satellite layer and the NWS forecast area, as uint8 0.1 m rasters (255 = no value). scripts/flood_3d.py adds both to existing bundles (done for fixture-flood, Calcasieu River, St Johns River). Contracts in contracts.py / floodTypes.ts / SPEC (5.3, 5.4, 6, 8.11, 10); SPEC's title, intro and every user-facing 'Fire-3d' renamed to Disaster Mapping.

relief.area_note: ground within 2 km of the mapped water (satellite water and the NWS forecast flooded area)
relief.rule: Height boost: the smallest of ×1.5, ×2, ×3, ×5, ×8 and ×10 that makes the middle 90% of the ground heights near the mapped water (5th to 95th percentile) span at least 2% of the area's width; ×1.5 when the ground is already steep enough. Only heights are boosted, never distances.

hand.label: Height above the river (from terrain). Not a flood map
hand.caveat: Height of the ground above the nearest river channel, from the terrain model and NOAA's river lines. It is not a flood map: low ground is not always flooded, and higher ground can flood (rain, small streams, drains). Experimental. Not an all-clear.
hand.method: NOAA National Water Model river lines (stream order 3 and up) are drawn on the terrain grid. Each channel cell takes the lowest terrain height within one cell of it; every other cell takes the height of its nearest channel cell in a straight line and shows how far above it the ground is (below it counts as 0). Cells more than 10 km from a channel are left out. Simplified from Height Above the Nearest Drainage (Nobre et al., 2011), which follows the downhill flow path instead: near a ridge between two valleys a cell can be measured against the other valley.
hand.citation: Nobre, A. D., et al. (2011). Height Above the Nearest Drainage, a hydrologically relevant new terrain model. Journal of Hydrology 404(1-2), 13-29.
hand.source: Terrain (USGS 3DEP) and river lines (NOAA National Water Model)

depth.label: Estimated depth (from the terrain at the water's edge), experimental
depth.caveat: Estimated depth inside the mapped water only: the water surface is taken from the terrain height along the water's edge and the ground is subtracted (the published FwDET method, Cohen et al.). Experimental: errors of a metre or more are common, most where the edge runs up a steep bank or the map and the terrain do not line up. The terrain model shows the river's normal water surface, not its bed, so depth in the normal channel is not measured. Shallow water here is not an all-clear. Follow local officials.
depth.method: Cells of the mapped water next to open ground are its edge (edges against clouds, no data, ocean or the area's border are not used). Each water cell takes the terrain height of its nearest edge cell as the water surface; depth = water surface − terrain, below 0 counts as 0, then a 3 × 3 average over the water smooths it (FwDET v2.0). Only cells inside the mapped water get a depth.
depth.citation: Cohen, S., et al. (2018). Estimating Floodwater Depths from Flood Inundation Maps and Topography. JAWRA 54(4), 847-858, doi:10.1111/1752-1688.12609. Cohen, S., et al. (2019). The Floodwater Depth Estimation Tool (FwDET v2.0) for improved remote sensing analysis of coastal flooding. NHESS 19, 2053-2065, doi:10.5194/nhess-19-2053-2019.
depth.source: Water seen by satellite (NASA OPERA), image of Oct 26, 2026, 11:49 AM EDT

manifest.layers.hand (St Johns River).description: Height above the nearest river channel (simplified HAND; NWM river lines of stream order 3 and up), 0.1 m steps, 254 = 25.4 m or more, 255 = no value

known_issues: Depth is estimated for the satellite pass the bundle shows (water_satellite) and the NWS forecast area only; the other kept passes (water_pass_*) have no depth raster, so the 3D water surface cannot follow every playback step (web-forensic-flood-3d: show it only for the shown pass or the forecast layer).

FwDET reads depth slightly low (the edge cells lie just inside the water: up to one cell's rise of the bank, ~0.3 m on a 1 % bank at 30 m) and errs by a metre or more on steep banks or misaligned maps; in hydro-flattened lidar the normal river channel reads near 0 m (its water surface, not its bed). Said in DEPTH_CAVEAT.

HAND is the straight-line simplification (nearest channel cell), not the flow-path HAND of Nobre et al.: near ridges a cell can be measured against the next valley; cells over 10 km from a stream of order 3+ have no value (a hard edge can show on very flat plains). Said in HAND_METHOD.

The satellite step of brief 5 can choose a pass with no clear view (clouds count as seen there); the timeline marks it no_view while shown_key still points at it (seen on the Grand River flood). Changing that choice belongs to floods/satellite.py (not this role).

Earthdata GIS loads passes 2-4 days after the overpass, so the newest days of a live flood often have no pass yet (the window still reaches now). With EARTHDATA_TOKEN, PO.DAAC passes (DSWx-S1 radar) are listed and read; that path is untested live (no token in this session).
Bundles grow with pass images: up to 8 MB more (St Johns 29.5 MB). The build test keeps its < 20 MB bound (the recorded flood has few passes); the new terrain test allows < 30 MB.
A cold /timeline call can take its full 20 s budget on floods with many passes (each read ~3 s, 3 at a time); the web should call with wait=0 and poll while complete is false.
